Middle East.headline: Syria, Jordan seek to mend ties after deadly airstrikes
Middle East.body: The foreign ministers of Syria and Jordan met in Damascus on Monday for the first time since Jordanian airstrikes killed civilians in southern Syria last month, announcing a joint investigation into the incident and signing 11 new co-operation agreements. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani said Jordan had shown understanding and openness towards resolving the incident in Deraa province, adding that the two countries had set up a joint security and technical committee to investigate the circumstances of the airstrikes. Americas.headline: Venezuela — Earthquakes Kill Over 1,700 and Prompt International Response
Americas.body: A pair of powerful earthquakes in north-central Venezuela has killed more than 1,700 people and injured nearly 1,000 others, with thousands reported missing. Rescue workers warn that the window to locate survivors beneath the rubble is closing. Venezuelan emergency teams are conducting intensive rescue operations, supported by search and rescue units dispatched by the United States and aid commitments from China and the European Union.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Mass Kidnapping and Lethal Attack Amid Escalating Gang Conflict
Americas.body: An attack by armed men in Kenscoff on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince killed at least 47 people, including five children, and resulted in the kidnapping of over 50 others, according to the United Nations. A gang leader threatened to execute hostages if security forces intervene. Simultaneously, Haitian security forces killed Boston gang leader Mathias Saintil in Cité Soleil during targeted operations utilizing explosive drones.

Americas.headline: Mexico — Investigation Launched After Child Killed in Security Operation
Americas.body: Mexican authorities are investigating military and police involvement in the fatal shooting of a seven-year-old American child in the border city of Matamoros. The death occurred during a joint security operation conducted to detain an alleged drug trafficker.

Africa.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 5,000 Deaths
Africa.body: An Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded to 10,910 confirmed cases and 5,234 confirmed deaths, making it the second largest and fastest growing on record. The current crude case-fatality rate is 48.7 percent. Doctors Without Borders has called for expanded deployment of the Ervebo vaccine to provide potential cross-protection against the Ebola Bundibugyo strain. Internationally, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is recruiting personnel to conduct airport screenings for travelers coming from Central Africa.

Africa.headline: Ethiopia / Kenya — Border Clashes Displace Over 50,000 People
Africa.body: Deadly clashes in the Moyale border region between Ethiopia and Kenya have displaced more than 50,000 people into Kenya. Displaced individuals reported burned homes and civilian casualties associated with tensions over flag displays in disputed areas. Families fleeing across the border are arriving without adequate shelter, food, cooking supplies, or bedding. Humanitarian concerns are escalating as displaced populations face severe hardship, with infants sleeping on bare floors and cases of diarrhoea spreading among affected groups.

Africa.headline: Sudan — Severe Drought Drives 90 Percent Crop Loss in Darfur
Africa.body: Nineteen agricultural emergency rooms in Darfur warn of widespread crop failure caused by drought and erratic rainfall. Human rights group Justice Africa Sudan projects harvest losses of around 90 percent across major sorghum-producing regions, raising severe concerns over impending famine. The organization called for an immediate nationwide ceasefire, full humanitarian access, and urgent emergency aid funding. Representatives described 2026 as one of the severe agricultural downturns in Sudan's recent history due to persistent low rainfall across large parts of the country.

Africa.headline: Somalia — Concurrent Outbreaks of Cholera, Measles, and Diphtheria
Africa.body: Public health researchers report that Somalia is confronting simultaneous outbreaks of cholera, measles, and diphtheria. Experts argue these overlapping health emergencies act as a syndemic driven by shared structural vulnerabilities. The crisis is heavily aggravated by widespread malnutrition, insufficient access to safe drinking water, and compromised sanitation systems across affected areas, severely challenging national public health responses.

Europe.headline: Ukraine/Russia — US-led peace negotiations open in Abu Dhabi
Europe.body: United States, Russian, and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi for trilateral talks aimed at negotiating an end to the war in Ukraine. The meetings represent the first substantive negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv since February. US officials stated they are seeking a final end to the conflict and proposing a long-term security architecture between Europe and Russia. US Senator Marco Rubio characterized the initial four-hour discussion as very productive, with negotiations expected to continue.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Unconfirmed tremors and explosion sounds reported across several cities
Europe.body: Residents across several regions in Ukraine, including Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, and Dnipro, reported underground tremors, loud rumblings, and sounds resembling explosions on 10 November. Eyewitnesses described shaking walls, swinging doors, and damaged plaster in some buildings. Unverified reports circulated on social media alleging a major underground explosion near Kyiv, but officials have not confirmed an earthquake or any direct cause for the vibrations.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar military airstrikes on schools in Sagaing kill 11
Asia-Pacific.body: Regime airstrikes on schools and residential houses in Kani and Taze townships in Sagaing Region over the weekend killed 11 civilians, including young children, and injured four others, according to the National Unity Government (NUG). On Saturday morning, three junta gyrocopters from the Monywa-based Northwestern Command bombed Nyaung Pin Lel village, located 13 miles southwest of Kani town. The bombs landed by the village school and nearby residential houses, killing eight civilians immediately. Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: MSF calls for broader access to ERVEBO vaccine during Ebola outbreak
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: As the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continues in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is calling for access to ERVEBO, the only licensed Ebola vaccine currently available at scale, to be expanded rapidly. MSF is urging the World Health Organization (WHO) Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE) to lift restrictions limiting ERVEBO vaccination to research protocols so that available doses can be deployed rapidly to protect those most at risk. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ghana mandates Ebola airport screening and 21-day tracking as Bundibugyo outbreak nears...
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Ghana has enforced mandatory electronic health declarations and a strict 21-day monitoring protocol for international arrivals, stepping up its defenses against the deadliest Ebola outbreak in recent history. The Ghana Health Service (GHS) intensified border controls at Kotoka International Airport and other entry points in early November 2026 to prevent the importation of the Bundibugyo virus. With the outbreak surpassing 9,700 cases in Central and East Africa and no licensed vaccine available, West African aviation hubs are relying on aggressive surveillance and traveler tracking to maintain open transit corridors while shielding domestic populations. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: How Ghana can prepare for possible Ebola outbreak
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The President of the Ghana Medical Association, Professor Yorke, has called for intensified public education, wider dissemination of information on quarantine and isolation facilities, improved case management preparedness, and stronger surveillance across relevant agencies to ensure the country is adequately prepared to respond to a possible Ebola outbreak. Speaking at a recent press conference to mark the close of its 68th Annual General Conference, the GMA President said Ghana must move beyond routine surveillance at the country's entry points and strengthen its capacity to respond to a possible outbreak.
